name: Filter media and housings
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
cross_reference: Cross-links to Category 8 (drinking water and beverages) and to the water-filters row; never pooled with the alloy-leach or glaze-leach bands of this category.
native_basis: element release from the treatment device into the treated water (µg/L, reported as µg/kg)
native_basis_label: NET ELEMENT RELEASE FROM THE TREATMENT DEVICE INTO THE TREATED WATER, µg/L reported as µg/kg, determined as device effluent minus a matched influent blank so that any contribution BY the device is resolved separately from what the device removes. This is a device-release basis on the water leaving the device; the sovereign drinking-water parametric values are a WATER basis on the supply as delivered and are disclosed as companions, never republished as the device's release ceiling.
scope_note: The media and housing components sold and replaced separately from the device. The media cell is unregulated in a way worth stating precisely: Reg (EU) 10/2011 does not merely omit ion-exchange resin, it EXPRESSLY EXCLUDES it by Art. 2(2)(a), and there is no EU specific measure for adsorbent media of any kind. Media are also the component that carries an inherent element load, since KDF-type media are a copper-zinc alloy, activated alumina is an aluminium compound, and mineral adsorbents carry raw-material impurities, so an unconditioned first draw from fresh media is the expected worst case and the conditioning instruction is part of what is certified. Plastic housings, sumps, end caps, O-rings and manifolds are NOT held to a separate published ceiling on this row. They are wetted components of a water-treatment device and are tested under the SAME net-device-contribution control as every other component, against a matched influent blank, with no separate number published. The alternative was considered and rejected on the record: reading the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics specific migration limits across onto the housing would import a FOOD-basis migration ceiling in ug/kg of food into a row whose declared native basis is net element release into the TREATED WATER, and mixing those two bases inside one row is the exact conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent. Where a housing polymer is separately placed on the market as a food-contact article in its own right, the plastics instrument governs it in that capacity as a distinct obligation, never as this row's ceiling. Spent media additionally hold the element load they removed, so change-out interval and end-of-life behaviour are certified requirements rather than advisory.
material: Activated carbon, granular and block, coconut- and coal-based; ion-exchange resin, cation and anion; KDF-type copper-zinc redox alloy; activated alumina; iron-oxide and titanium-oxide adsorbents; diatomaceous earth and ceramic elements; RO and UF membranes with polysulfone supports; plastic cartridge housings, sumps, end caps, O-rings and manifolds.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) each MEDIUM as its own lot, extraction at first draw and after the stated conditioning volume, against a matched influent blank; (2) KDF-type copper-zinc alloy media, with alloy composition verified for lead, cadmium and nickel impurity; (3) activated alumina and aluminium-bearing media, tested specifically for aluminium net contribution; (4) mineral, ceramic and diatomaceous media, tested for arsenic and heavy-metal raw-material load; (5) ION-EXCHANGE RESIN, expressly outside Reg (EU) 10/2011 by Art. 2(2)(a), tested for both element release and resin-fine carryover; (6) plastic housing, sump, end cap, O-ring and manifold, under the same net-device-contribution control as every other wetted component, with no separate ceiling published and no plastics-migration read-across; (7) SPENT media at and beyond rated capacity, for release of accumulated element load; (8) any metal insert, mesh, spring or fitting in the wetted path.
basis_guard: release into (the )?treated water|treated[ -]water|device effluent|net device contribution|effluent
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as NET ELEMENT RELEASE FROM THE TREATMENT DEVICE INTO THE TREATED WATER may anchor a cell on this row. A sovereign drinking-water parametric value is deliberately NOT admitted by this guard: it is a WATER basis on the supply as delivered, and republishing it as the device's own release ceiling is the precise conflation this row exists to prevent. It is disclosed as a companion obligation instead. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap. DECLARED VACUOUS STATE (recorded, not overlooked): as written this guard matches ZERO live, non-draft and non-quarantined rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and that is its intended state. The release regime this row's basis family belongs to is not in the register in any form this row may bind, which is the same fact this row's control cells record and state in detail; a guard that admitted a live row today could only do so by admitting a foreign basis. The guard is nevertheless expressed in the register's own basis vocabulary (element or specific release, release into food or a food simulant, 4 percent acetic acid extract, per dm2 of food-contact surface, net device contribution to the treated water) so that a future correct ingest of that regime BINDS through it. The previous prose-sentence guard on this row would have REJECTED the very instruments it was waiting for and forced them to a gap, which is the defect this rewrite removes. Two limits on the guard's force are stated plainly rather than left implicit: the compiler returns on the control branch before basis resolution, so a guard is never evaluated on a control cell, and this note rather than the machine is what carries the guard's force on this row today. The engine change that would close that hole - an assertion that every declared basis_guard either matches at least one live register row or carries basis_guard_vacuous_by_design, failing the build otherwise - is recorded as a tooling gap and is outside this config's scope.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.
